At the **SMaLL** research group, our work lies at the intersection of statistics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. We are driven by a dual mission: to push the boundaries of AI by developing novel, powerful, and principled methods, and to solve pressing real-world problems across a range of scientific and societal domains.

Our research is grounded in a deep understanding of statistical theory, which allows us to build machine learning models that are not only accurate but also reliable, interpretable, and robust. We focus on three core areas: developing trustworthy AI, advancing core ML methodologies, and applying these innovations to achieve interdisciplinary impact.

### Trustworthy & Reliable AI: Uncertainty, Interpretability, and Calibration

A central theme of our research is moving beyond simple point predictions to create AI systems that understand and communicate their own uncertainty. We believe this is essential for applications in science, medicine, and beyond.

- **Uncertainty Quantification & Conformal Prediction**:
  We develop cutting-edge techniques for creating statistically valid prediction intervals and confidence sets. Our work, including methods like [**CD-split**](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v23/20-797.html) and [**EPICSCore**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v286/cruz-cabezas25a.html), provides rigorous, assumption-free uncertainty guarantees via conformal methods, even for complex, high-dimensional data. Recent work broadens this toolkit along several axes: [**CREDO**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06826) builds conformalized credal envelopes that separate epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty, [**LoBoost**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22432) delivers fast model-native local intervals for gradient-boosted trees, [**LOCUS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01971) targets risk-aware predictions through a distribution-free loss-quantile score, and we extend valid prediction regions to [compositional data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18141) and [skewed responses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16145).

- **Interpretability and Explainable AI (XAI)**:
  We design methods to open the "black box" of complex models like neural networks. Our work on meaningful local explanations (e.g., [**MeLIME**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.05818), [**RFFNet**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.06410), and [**NLS**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05206)) helps users understand why a model makes a particular decision, fostering trust and enabling model debugging.

- **Model Diagnostics and Calibration**:
  We create tools for rigorously validating and diagnosing machine learning models. This includes techniques for likelihood-free inference (e.g., [**WALDO**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.15680), [**LF2I**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03920)) and diagnostics for conditional density models ([**LaDaR**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.14568)), ensuring reliable and well-calibrated probabilistic outputs. We are extending these ideas to generative models used as scientific simulators ([trustworthy scientific inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02602)), to locally calibrated credible sets in simulation-based inference ([**CP4SBI**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17077)), and to [rare events, via diagnostic transport maps](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.11229).

### Core Methodological Advances in Machine Learning

Our foundational work aims to create more flexible, powerful, and efficient learning algorithms.

- **Conditional Density Estimation (CDE)**:
  A cornerstone of our research is the development of nonparametric methods for estimating full outcome distributions given features. Our [**FlexCode**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08095) procedure, used by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, is one such example applied in astronomy and beyond. More recently, we have been benchmarking and adapting [**tabular foundation models**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.26611) for CDE, bringing this new generation of pretrained models to bear on distributional prediction.

- **Network Science & Graph-based Learning**:
  We develop methods for [community detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.05909), [hypothesis testing on graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06478), and [network modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.08880), with applications ranging from EEG brain data to social networks. Current work targets weighted and sparse networks, including [counting communities in weighted stochastic block models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15891), [sparsity-aware models for count-weighted networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03100), and [normalized likelihood criteria for model selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10205).

- **High-Dimensional & Nonparametric Methods**:
  We specialize in “large \( p \), small \( n \)” problems, using spectral series, wavelets, and kernel methods. We also design efficient algorithms like [**ExactBoost**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v151/csillag22a.html) and [**BlockBoost**](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v238/ramos24a.html) for challenging ML tasks.

- **Modern AI Architectures**:
  We contribute to model ensembling ([**NN-Stacking**](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09735)), scalable kernel methods ([**RFFNet**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.06410)), and the use of variational autoencoders for high-dimensional hypothesis testing.

- **Causal Inference**:
  We develop nonparametric methods for estimating causal effects from observational data, including approaches based on the [front-door criterion](https://openreview.net/forum?id=1c6A74tLOd) for settings with unmeasured confounding.

### Interdisciplinary Impact: AI in Action

We are passionate about applying our methods to solve concrete problems. Our collaborations span:

- **Astronomy & Cosmology**:
  [Photo-z estimation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11523), galaxy classification, and [likelihood-free cosmological inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.11523).

- **Healthcare & Medicine**:
  [Predicting mortality](https://doi.org/10.1590/0102-311X00050818), [diagnosing dementia](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1041610215001982) and Parkinson’s (e.g., [**Goalkeeper Game**](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnagi.2020.00050)), [modeling infectious diseases](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pntd.0012501), and AI tools for breast cancer risk ([**PersonalizedUS**](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/35017)).

- **Genetics & Genomics**:
  [QTL mapping](https://doi.org/10.1534/genetics.115.180802), [feature selection for ALS studies](https://doi.org/10.3390/jpm12081330), and interaction detection in complex traits.

- **Ecology & Environmental Science**:
  Biodiversity quantification, species composition analysis ([**LDAcov**](https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.7626)), and population modeling.

- **Law, Social Science & Sports Analytics**:
  Quantifying legal [“loss of a chance”](https://doi.org/10.1093/lpr/mgz010), modeling judicial decisions, and [predicting football match outcomes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04356).

- **Computational Neuroscience**:
  Modeling spiking activity with stochastic chains of variable-length memory: [inferring effective connectivity between neurons](https://doi.org/10.3390/brainsci14050442), [consistently selecting models of functional interaction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08205), and [identifying astrocytic signatures in neuronal recordings](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11571-025-10276-4).

- **Insurance & Actuarial Science**:
  [Actuarial learning for pension-fund mortality forecasting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.05881) and conformal prediction for [frequency–severity modeling](https://doi.org/10.1080/02664763.2025.2567988) of insurance claims.

- **Materials Science**:  
  Predicting properties of glass materials to guide new compositions, [quantifying oxide glass similarity through learned distances](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnoncrysol.2026.124303), [building datasets by mining patents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16366), and [automating the microscopic analysis of cement clinker](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2025.128552) — always incorporating uncertainty for robust scientific inference.

### Bayesian Foundations and Logical Coherence

Our approach is deeply Bayesian and committed to logical rigor. We believe this foundation leads to better, more coherent statistical and AI models.

- **Foundations of Inference**:
  We explore [statistical decision theory](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10260-019-00486-6), [value of information](https://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/philosophy/docs/seidenfeld/the-utility-of-a-scientific-explanation,-for-submission-v2.pdf), and [imprecise probability models](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijar.2022.08.016).

- **Logically-Consistent Hypothesis Testing**:
  We develop coherent frameworks for multiple hypothesis testing that avoid contradictions. Tools like [**REACT**](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09112) support interpretable and practical alternatives to p-values.

Here is a list of our papers from the last 5 years — the complete list can be downloaded <a href="https://github.com/small-research/website/raw/main/references.csv" download>here</a>.



```{python}
import pandas as pd
import html
from IPython.display import display, HTML
from datetime import datetime


current_year = int(datetime.now().year)
initial_date = current_year - 5

def print_paper_table():
    # Lê o arquivo CSV
    paper_table = pd.read_csv("references.csv")

    # Filtra e ordena os dados
    paper_table = paper_table[paper_table['Year'] >= initial_date].sort_values(by='Year', ascending=False)

    # Cria a coluna de conteúdo formatada em HTML
    paper_table['content'] = (
        paper_table['Authors'].fillna('').apply(html.escape) +
        ". <b>" + paper_table['Title'].fillna('').apply(html.escape) +
        "</b>. " + paper_table['Publication'].fillna('').apply(html.escape)
    )

    search_box = """
    <div class="pub-search">
      <input type="search" id="pub-search-input" class="form-control"
             placeholder="Search by author, title, or venue..."
             oninput="filterPubTable()" aria-label="Search publications">
      <div id="pub-search-count" class="pub-search-count"></div>
    </div>
    """

    # Gera o HTML da tabela (sem paginação, como pageLength = -1 no R)
    html_table = "<div class='table-responsive'><table id='pub-table' class='pub-table'>"
    for _, row in paper_table.iterrows():
        html_table += f"<tr><td class='pub-year'>{int(row['Year'])}</td><td>{row['content']}</td></tr>"
    html_table += "</table></div>"

    script = """
    <script>
    function filterPubTable() {
      var input = document.getElementById('pub-search-input');
      var filter = input.value.toLowerCase();
      var rows = document.querySelectorAll('#pub-table tr');
      var visible = 0;
      rows.forEach(function(row) {
        var match = row.textContent.toLowerCase().indexOf(filter) > -1;
        row.style.display = match ? '' : 'none';
        if (match) visible++;
      });
      var count = document.getElementById('pub-search-count');
      count.textContent = filter ? (visible + ' of ' + rows.length + ' papers') : '';
    }
    </script>
    """

    display(HTML(search_box + html_table + script))

```


```{python}
 print_paper_table()
```
